title: A Generalist Hanabi Agent
abstract: arXiv:2503.14555v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) systems can develop cooperative strategies through repeated interactions. However, these systems are unable to perform well on any other setting than the one they have been trained on, and struggle to successfully cooperate with unfamiliar collaborators. This is particularly visible in the Hanabi benchmark, a popular 2-to-5 player cooperative card-game which requires complex reasoning and precise assistance to other agents. Current MARL agents for Hanabi can only learn one specific game-setting (e.g., 2-player games), and play with the same algorithmic agents. This is in stark contrast to humans, who can quickly adjust their strategies to work with unfamiliar partners or situations. translated_abstract: 传统的多智能体强化学习（MARL）系统可以通过反复交互发展出合作策略。然而，这些系统在训练设置之外的其他环境中无法有良好表现，并且难以与不熟悉的合作者成功协作。这一点在Hanabi基准测试中尤为明显——Hanabi是一个流行的2至5人合作卡牌游戏，需要复杂的推理以及对其他智能体的精确协助。目前用于Hanabi的MARL智能体只能学习单一特定的游戏设置（例如双人游戏），并且只能与相同的算法智能体一起游戏。这与人类形成了鲜明对比——人类可以快速调整自己的策略，以适应不熟悉的伙伴或情境。在本文中，我们提出了循环回放相关性分布式DQN（Recurrent Replay Relevance Distributed DQN，R3D2），这是一种为克服上述限制而设计的通用型Hanabi智能体。我们使用文本形式重新构建了该任务，将其作为语言……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出了通用型Hanabi智能体R3D2（循环回放相关性分布式DQN），通过将游戏任务以文本形式重新构建，使单个智能体能够应对多种游戏设置并与陌生伙伴协作，突破了传统多智能体强化学习只能适应单一训练场景的局限。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces R3D2 (Recurrent Replay Relevance Distributed DQN), a generalist Hanabi agent that reformulates the game as a text-based task, enabling a single agent to handle multiple game settings and cooperate with unfamiliar partners, overcoming the limitations of traditional MARL systems.
